title: There is no maintained, freely-licensed Camunda edition to integrate with
content:
Two facts combine into one conclusion. Camunda 7 Community reached its final feature release on 14 October 2025, after which *"the repository will be archived shortly after. After this date, no further releases, including security patches, will be made"* — and the GitHub API confirms `archived: true`. Enterprise received an extension to 2030; Community did not.

Camunda 8's licence grants use *"only and limited to the Use in or for the purpose of Using the Software in Non-Production Environment"*, defined to exclude *"any live or production systems"*, with the alternative stated bluntly: *"You must purchase a commercial license ... or You must refrain from Using the Software."* The key may not be *"move[d], change[d], disable[d], or circumvent[ed]"*.

So the only Apache-2.0 Camunda is unpatched abandonware and the only maintained Camunda is production-forbidden without payment. For a buyer under BSI or NIS2 obligations each is disqualifying in a different way. Note the asymmetry that survives: the Exporter API — the natural integration seam — is Apache-2.0, while the engine it exports from is not.
description: The Apache-2.0 build was archived in October 2025 with no further security patches, and the maintained build grants production use only on purchase.
